reason: RQ2: extends — predates AgentHER and applies HER to LM agents via hindsight subgoal-rule + compressed trajectory memory; useful as the upstream lineage point for the L2 relabeling note but does not yet produce DPO/SFT data packaging.

RQ3: extends — instrumentation-free eBPF boundary tracing with TLS interception at <3% overhead is an alternative L0 path orthogonal to AgentTrace's in-process schema; relevant cost-control reference for the observability tax discussion.

RQ3: extends — runtime-log-driven flow discovery and analytics taxonomy for agentic systems; secondary reference for L0/L1 since it stays at the analytics level without specifying schema fields or sentinel triggers.

RQ5: supports — 1,302-trace meta-evaluation of 12 LLM judges shows no judge dominates and rule-based eval underreports success; useful empirical evidence behind the 'judging accuracy ≠ triage informativeness' thesis claim.
RQ3: supports — systematic-mapping taxonomy of artifacts to trace across the agent lifecycle; provides a comparison frame for AgentTrace's three-surface schema rather than new schema fields.

RQ1: extends — Siamese Recurrent Autoencoder over action plans gives a sequence-level non-semantic detector at 32 ms / 17–27× faster than LLM-judge with F1 0.88–0.94 on real failure benchmarks (RAS-Eval, Who&When), filling the deployable L1 detector slot Signals leaves abstract.

RQ5: supports — empirical evidence (kappa=0.049 substring, only moderate three-LLM ensemble agreement) corroborates thesis that LLM-as-Judge cannot be a front-line filter; runtime interceptor (-23pp hallucination on GPT-4o-mini) is a useful mitigation primitive.

RQ3: extends — typed transducible functions with evidence tracing between input/output slots offer a schema-validity + locality-of-evidence primitive complementary to AgentTrace's three-surface model; potentially useful as L0 type-system grounding.

RQ1: extends — a 12-category error taxonomy across tool initialization/parameter/execution/result-interpretation phases (1980 deterministic scenarios) is a useful complement to KWeaver's L1 execution-signal class; mostly catalog rather than detector design.

RQ6: orthogonal — 14-mode MAS taxonomy (specification / inter-agent misalignment / task verification, kappa=0.88, 1600 traces) is heavily MAS-coordination focused; useful for vocabulary but not directly transferable to single-agent KWeaver scope.

RQ5: orthogonal — local anomaly detection + backward symptom tracing for MAS root-cause attribution; the symptom-tracing pattern is suggestive for L1 sentinel triggers but the framework targets inter-agent dependencies KWeaver does not have.

RQ1: extends — PolicyGuardBench (60k examples) and PolicyGuard-4B occupy the small-surrogate tier between rule-based Signals and LLM-as-Judge; prefix-based detection is the closest published analogue to KWeaver L1's anticipatory-trigger requirement.

RQ1: supports — XGBoost (98%) and SVDD (96%) on a 4275-trajectory benchmark of drift/cycle/missing-detail failures reinforces the lightweight non-LLM detector path; methodology is conventional ML rather than novel mechanism, so skim-tier.

RQ1: extends — provenance-based hierarchical execution-unit constraints + behavioral consistency checks sit between AgentSeer (action-component graph) and Sentinel (KG invariants); valuable contrast for L1 mechanism design but secondary to top deep-read picks this run.

RQ1: extends — fine-grained process-supervision verifier with step-level localization for rollback-and-retry; uses a fine-tuned LLM verifier (heavier than thesis's preferred small-surrogate tier), so skim as a contrast on cost/granularity tradeoff.

RQ1: supports — empirical 8-17% latent-failure rate in correct-outcome trajectories on tau2-Airlines directly validates the thesis claim that successful traces contain learnable hidden friction; introduces ToolGuard executable-policy detection as a small-surrogate L1 mechanism distinct from existing notes.
